- Success metrics: JSON schema compliance >= 98% for critical fields, mean token latency < 150ms on p95, and end-to-end accuracy on intent classification >= 92% on the provided prompt set.
- Immediate asks from your side: share a representative prompt set (you mentioned ~1k examples) and confirm if we can run a short eval on anonymized production-similar data.

What I'm proposing next (2-week focused eval):
1) We run our standard model-fit evals (structured-output + tool-calling scenarios) against the prompt set you provide.
2) We return a benchmark report with per-model tradeoffs (latency/cost/JSON compliance) and recommended quantization/serving configs.
3) Technical deep-dive with Rishi (our lead on structured output) to walk through results and an obs-driven rollout plan.

Appreciate the quick reply, Alex - and thanks for the security questions attachment. Below are concrete answers and the recommended plan for the structured-output/tool-calling portion of the eval.

1) Drop the prompt set in the Drive folder (link below) and I'll confirm ingestion by EOD. We'll anonymize and hash any PII before evaluation.

2) Recommended models for your use case (tradeoffs summarized):
   - redwood-v2-medium (quantized int8): strong structured-output accuracy, lowest latency baseline. Good for high-throughput use cases.
   - redwood-v2-large (8-bit + KV caching): better instruction-following and tool orchestration for multi-step flows. Higher cost but higher JSON compliance.
   - open-llama-13b (quant-llm): cost-effective for batch workloads; consider for async processing.

3) JSON schema compliance & retries (runtime approach):
   - Validation: we run both a lightweight runtime validator (fast JSON schema check) and a deeper fuzz + schema-check during eval. We report field-level compliance rates and examples of common failures.
   - Retry policy: for transient parse failures we recommend up to 2 automatic deterministic retries with: (a) prompt-engineered repair (explicit "Return valid JSON per schema X. If you cannot, output: {\"error\":\"PARSE_FAILURE\"}\"), (b) backoff 200ms -> 400ms for the second retry, and (c) fall back to a structured extraction heuristic if retries fail.
   - Tool/function calling: our runtime supports annotated function signatures + strict return-type checks. On mismatch we surface the raw function output and the model output side-by-side in the eval report.

4) Deliverables from our 2-week eval:
   - Benchmark CSV: per-model token cost, p50/p95 latency, JSON compliance by field.
   - Prompt set + annotated failure cases report.
   - Suggested serving config (model, quantization, batch settings, cache TTLs).

Attachments included: avery_prompt_set_v1.json (template), model_recommendations.csv (summary table).

Looping in with a proposed technical plan for the JSON/schema + function-calling eval (I'll run the initial harness):

- Eval focus: 1) JSON schema compliance (field-level), 2) function/tool-calling correctness and idempotency, 3) failure modes (malformed JSON, partial outputs, hallucinated tool calls).
- Test harness: we use a replayable harness that feeds your prompts deterministically and records model outputs + runtime traces (timestamps, kernels used, cache hits).
- Schema checks: runtime validator then a post-run fuzzy-check to capture borderline cases (e.g., numeric fields serialized as strings).
- Retry implementation we'll test: up to 2 deterministic retries with explicit repair prompt. We'll capture whether retries improve schema compliance and the cost delta.
- Deliver an "eval_plan.md" into the Drive folder and share a short README for reproducing results locally.

I'll bring initial results to the 10am PT call. If anyone wants a pre-reads thread, I can drop the eval_plan.md now.

Thanks,
